paper.central_claim: A coding-agent loop that watches a robot fail, writes skills or installs external models and tests every change in simulation, run for 123 rounds on RoboCasa household tasks, discovered real capabilities (active viewing) but its improvements did not add up: the target fridge task never succeeded. The agent was rarely the bottleneck; three surrounding factors were: chained perception modules do not represent relations (semantic displacement), skill chains lock learning onto the first step, and the harness (evaluators, gates, memory) decides what the agent learns.
paper.title: What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery

signatures.object: The robot's software library (task programs, skills with typed implementations and routing rules, external perception/planning model providers) improved by Codex-CLI GPT agents; before-state is the library at round t.
signatures.information: Proposer sees the failure table, the evaluator's diagnosis (derived from privileged simulator state), execution traces and diffs of earlier attempts and RGB keyframes of failed steps; the robot perceives via head and wrist RGB-D and joint readings; the harness (evaluators, tests, memory, actuator description) is editable only by humans.
signatures.operation: Collect rollouts -> evaluator judges declared steps -> group first failures into gaps -> proposer writes code or files a model request -> research agent installs/probes/registers models -> test and accept -> next round starts from the improved library; routing refit from logged calls.
signatures.output: Accepted skill changes (57), registered providers (86), refitted routing, new task programs.
signatures.conditions: RoboCasa kitchen, PandaOmron mobile manipulator; Fridge (about 15 steps), Cabinet, Sink; four scene seeds; one simulator and layout.
signatures.feedback: Evaluator diagnoses and traces; rejected attempts return execution traces after later harness repairs.
signatures.selection_rule: Replay the exact recorded failure, then paired old-vs-new trials on fresh scenes and a held-out task; later sealed transfer states and regression/invariance checks; thresholds and reproduction rules were revised by humans during the run.
signatures.persistence: Library and routing on disk, orchestrator keeps its best programs; typed memory of hypotheses added later.
signatures.later_use: Next-round rollouts of the three tasks; held-out cabinet-to-counter used only in gates.
signatures.claimed_effect: No gain at the task level: Fridge 0/486, Cabinet 0/256, Sink 14/230 (9 with failed intermediate steps) despite 57 accepted changes; retained local wins (round 118 grasp) did not move task success.
signatures.failure_boundary: Evaluator capture, noisy and under-resolved gates, evidence fixed point, lost requests, registered models never called, human repairs of 113 harness faults.

gap.author_gap: Coding agents improve software in loops (Voyager, Eureka, DGM) and the idea has reached robots (RHO, ASPIRE, ENPIRE); the paper asks whether such loops compound on a household manipulation task and, if not, what stops them and whether a stronger agent would fix it.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and consequential: positive reports exist, but a long fully recorded failing run with measured mechanisms is a distinct, falsifiable contribution. The conditions are framed after the fact from one run.
lineage: RHO, ASPIRE, ENPIRE (robot self-improvement with coding agents)
gap.closest_adjacent: ASPIRE (diagnosable traces, validated skill library) and ENPIRE (reset and verification module) report large gains; the authors read these as consistent with the harness deciding what the agent can achieve.
gap.residue: Open-instruction relational perception, long skill chains, and harness-side learning in a fully recorded robot loop.
gap.stakes: Accepted-change counts measure activity, not progress; human harness repair outnumbers accepted changes about two to one.
gap.method_response: A fully instrumented 123-round run plus a three-condition analysis and falsifiable recommendations.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether the recommendations (D1-D12) work; replicates, other agents and budgets; real robots.
unresolved: Whether a different proposer or budget would have solved the task is explicitly unknown.

claims.text: The loop's improvements did not add up: the target task never succeeded despite 57 accepted changes.
claims.setting: RoboCasa Fridge, Cabinet and Sink tasks, four scene seeds each, 123 rounds, GPT agents via Codex CLI.
claims.selection_vs_test: Gates used fresh scenes and a held-out task; reported outcomes are native task success in later rounds.
claims.result: Fridge 0/486, Cabinet 0/256, Sink 14/230 with 9 having failed intermediate steps; 57 accepted changes (51 perception).
counterevidence: Phase 1 produced a deployed active-search skill and eight called models.
claims.allowed_conclusion: In this run, accepted changes produced no task-level gain on Fridge and Cabinet.

claims.text: Semantic displacement: a code-writing agent fills the missing relational semantics with growing geometric rules that never converge.
claims.setting: Fridge region grounding; 27 attempts on a two-state gap.
claims.baseline: A 7B VLM queried on recorded views (feasibility only).
claims.result: 33 thresholds in 3,056 lines; rescue of one seed in all trials and none of the other; VLM correct in 4/4 recorded views.
counterevidence: VLM check covers a handful of views, not a benchmark.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Consistent with displacement for this front; generality is a hypothesis.

claims.text: Frontier lock: learning concentrates on the first failing step of a chain.
claims.result: 57% of fridge rollouts fail step 1; 0.9% pass five steps; round-118 grasp win reproduced but followed by 0/60 task successes.
counterevidence: No intervention such as resetting past the frontier was run.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Evidence is concentrated at the first steps, and a retained local gain did not reach the task.

claims.text: What the agent learns is decided by the harness (evaluator capture, unresolvable gates, evidence fixed point, memory corruption, capability not use, framing).
claims.result: 276 reachable successes within 1 mm of a 0.85 m sphere; 16/36 disagreeing pairs not reproduced; identical outcomes in rounds 90-102; 11 models never called; 0/8 vs 11/12 edits after a prompt paragraph changed.
counterevidence: The framing result is confounded with the round.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Several harness-side faults demonstrably shaped what the loop optimised; the relative weight of harness versus proposer is not established.

claims.text: The agent was rarely the bottleneck.
claims.result: Raising reasoning effort 'changed nothing visible'; no alternative agent run.
counterevidence: The authors state they cannot say whether a different agent, more compute or a different library representation would have solved the task.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not established as a causal claim.

claims.text: The agent can discover a missing capability from failures alone.
claims.setting: Phase 1 (rounds 1-36) after the evaluator reported target visibility.
claims.result: Active-viewing model requested, repaired and wrapped; out-of-view failures disappeared by round 16.
counterevidence: Required an evaluator fix by humans first.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop RoboCasa task success per rollout (native simulator success, with intermediate-step audit); step evaluator uses privileged state; no real robot; claim is negative.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In one 123-round run on three RoboCasa tasks with GPT agents, 57 accepted library changes and 86 provider registrations produced no Fridge (0/486) or Cabinet (0/256) successes and only mostly accidental Sink successes (14/230); records measure evaluator capture, evidence concentrated at the first chain step, gates noisier than effects, lost research requests and uncalled models. These mechanisms are identified from records, not tested causally; the claim that the agent was rarely the bottleneck is an interpretation of one run.
not_supported: that a stronger agent would not fix the task
relative effect sizes of the three lessons
generality beyond one simulator, one layout and three tasks
assessment.retained_improver_online_transfer: retained: accepted changes persist (library) but do not improve the task, so retained improvement is negative/unshown; improver: not shown; online: yes; transfer: no.
assessment.claim_type_note: system_method with a negative/diagnostic central claim (SCORE_SPEC: negative/audit papers judged on whether their central claim is supported). Not evaluation_resource: no benchmark, environment or evaluation method is contributed for reuse, and the paper calls itself a report of one experiment (agg:A01). Anchors precedent 3: type follows the self-described central claim.
unresolved: independent runs / layouts and matched agent budgets
separating agent, harness and provider co-variation
independent audit of the repaired step evaluator

G.reason: Resolved for son55 (4) over sol (3). A specific, consequential question (does software-style self-improvement compound for robots, and what stops it) is sourced by in-paper measurements; lineage (Voyager, Eureka, DGM) and the nearest robot systems (RHO, ASPIRE, ENPIRE) are named and differentiated (positive gains vs a fully recorded failing run), and the remaining gap is explicitly bounded (single run, remedies untested, Table 3 falsifiers). sol's reason for 3 was that neighbour originals are not in the fixed package, which holds for every paper and is not a defect of the positioning.

M.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. The three-condition framework and chain-attenuation identity give distinguishable, falsifiable predictions tied to measured fronts; they are post hoc from one run and declared non-predictive.

X.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Roles, information access, gates, model eras, round cadence and the human-repair rule are reconstructable with round-by-round records; harness, thresholds and agent configuration changed during the run; prompts/code not provided.

measurement.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Native simulator task success with explicit denominators that reconcile across tables (486+256+230=972 completed; 14 successes; 57 accepted), an audit of accidental Sink successes, and per-claim measurements (Table 5); the privileged step evaluator was itself repaired many times, so step diagnoses shifted over time.

causality.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Several mechanisms are directly measured (sphere-surface parking, uncalled models, lost requests, non-reproducing pairs), but there are no controls, replicates, matched baselines or ablations and the timeline is confounded (model switches at rounds 76/85, 113 harness repairs).

holdout.reason: Revised to 2 (sol 1, son55 3), chosen from the anchor text, not as a midpoint. Anchor 2 = "development overlaps evaluation, or held-out gain ~0": task outcomes are measured on the same four deterministic seeds per task that the loop collected failures from, the held-out task was visible to the agent until round 74, and the one held-out local win (round 118) produced zero task gain. Above 1 because a held-out task, fresh scenes and sealed states were actually used as gates and the authors confine the claim to one simulator/layout/three tasks; below 3 because no positive held-out generalization or independent run backs the general lessons stated in the abstract.

statistics.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Exact per-round and aggregate counts with first-failure denominators and a reproducibility check of paired differences (16/36 not reproduced); single run, four seeds, no intervals.

cost.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Time per round, attempt limits, model eras and 113 human repairs are reported; no token/USD/GPU totals or budget comparison.

status_reason: Complete fixed text including Appendices A-E read; all eight items resolved.
initial_evidence_judgment: Read in full before seat rating reasons. GPT agents (Codex CLI: orchestrator, multimodal proposer shown failure keyframes, research agent) rewrite a RoboCasa mobile manipulator's skill library and install external models from evaluator-diagnosed failures; changes pass replay, paired fresh-scene and held-out-task gates; humans may repair only the harness (evaluators, gates, memory, actuator description). One 123-round run: Fridge 0/486, Cabinet 0/256, Sink 14/230 (9 accidental); 57 accepted changes (51 perception), 86 provider registrations, 847 proposals, 113 human harness repairs. Mechanisms are measured from records (276 reach successes on a 0.85 m sphere surface; 57% fail step 1; 16/36 re-run pairs not reproduced; 88 requests gated as code; 11 late models never called; 33-threshold region skill). Explicitly no replicates, matched baselines or ablations; agent model changed twice mid-run; collection reused four deterministic seeds per task; held-out task hidden from the agent only from round 74. Contribution is a negative/diagnostic report with a three-condition framework and falsifiable design implications. Initial judgment: in scope (coding agents self-improving an embodied harness), claim type system_method (negative study of the authors' own system; no benchmark/resource contributed), online, claim scoped to mechanisms identified from one run.
base_seat_note: signatures/gap/claims are taken from the base seat unless overridden (ids namespaced); expectations are the base list plus the other seat's additional ids, with aggregate overrides marked aggregate_note.

resolutions.reason: Anchors precedent 3: type follows the self-described central claim - a report of running the authors' own self-improvement system and why it failed (agg:A01). No benchmark/environment/evaluation method is offered for reuse, and SCORE_SPEC's evaluation_resource reading (M = how tasks/metrics/verifiers fix a defect; X = protocol/annotation execution) does not fit an untested recommendations list. Negative claims are judged on support under either type (SCORE_SPEC).
resolutions.score_impact: none directly (same formula); fixes the interpretation of G/M/X

resolutions.reason: Sec 4 names the software-RSI assumptions and shows each violated in measurement; C02's defining move (controlled instances isolating one confound with an independent oracle) is absent - the paper says it is not a controlled study (sol itself marked single-axis isolation unmet).
The system built and run is a distinct operation that executes C25 (code artifacts gated by replay/fresh tests); fit lowered to partial because the gate proved unsound.
Primary assumption_audit_and_pivot with sub null (no C01-C29 tactic fits); supporting decompose_and_delegate with rs:C25 (its singleton). C02 removed with its main.
Question, lineage, nearest neighbours and remaining-gap boundary all explicit; sol's deduction rests on the package not containing neighbour originals, which is not a paper defect.

Task outcomes on reused seeds the loop learned from; held-out task visible until round 74; held-out local win gave zero task gain - anchor 2. son55's 3 overstates (no positive held-out generalization); sol's 1 ignores that held-out/fresh/sealed gates were really used and claims are explicitly confined.

R05 fits the operation (robot code rewritten from diagnostics, no agent at run time). K401 rejected because its revised object is the agent harness, which here is human-only (son55's own condition check). K804 partial because categories came from a repeatedly repaired evaluator.
